name: Few-View Reconstruction via Regularization
text:
# Few-View Reconstruction via Regularization


## Overview
Few-View Reconstruction via Regularization is a family of approaches designed to mitigate the shape-radiance ambiguity inherent in [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) and [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) when supervision from multiple viewpoints is sparse [S1, unofficial][S2]. By applying geometric or semantic priors, these methods prevent overfitting to observed views and improve generalization to unseen ones [S1, unofficial]. This family addresses artifacts like "floaters" and "background collapse" common in sparse-input settings [S2]. Unlike [progressive reconstruction](#20926-progressive-reconstruction.md) methods that restrain model capacity over time, this family relies on [explicit regularization](#18380-feature-grid-optimization-explicit-vs-implicit-regularizatio.md) terms to guide the optimization toward geometrically plausible solutions [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves augmenting the standard photometric loss with auxiliary constraints that enforce consistency across views or adherence to prior knowledge about scene geometry [S1, unofficial]. Geometric priors stabilize the learned density field or Gaussian distribution by applying smoothness or [normal consistency](#3050-normal-consistency.md) constraints [S1, unofficial]. Semantic regularization enforces cross-view consistency by leveraging high-level scene structure to align reconstructions with expected object layouts [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### Unseen Viewpoint Regularization
Unseen Viewpoint Regularization is a module designed to mitigate background collapse and overfitting in sparse-input settings by regularizing 3DGS training at viewpoints different from the input views [S2]. It is chosen when training data is extremely sparse and standard photometric loss leads to artifacts like floaters or empty backgrounds [S2]. The method splits regularization based on the distance of the novel view from training cameras [S2]. For viewpoints distant from training cameras, it incorporates a [Score Distillation Sampling (SDS)](#21179-score-distillation-sampling-sds.md) loss to provide geometric priors [S2]. For viewpoints close to training cameras, it incorporates a depth warping loss, which uses traditional transformations to re-render depth and color from novel view points and enforces consistency [S2].

## Background
The challenge of reconstructing scenes from sparse views is critical in real-world settings where dense multi-view captures are impractical [S1, unofficial]. Early solutions focused on constraining variation between views, such as [DietNeRF](#22404-dietnerf.md), which added constraints to ensure high-level semantic features remained the same across views [S2]. More recently, with the advent of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md), methods like [SparseGS](#6135-sparsegs.md) have introduced specific modules like Unseen Viewpoint Regularization to address the unique artifacts of [Gaussian representations](#5918-gaussian-based-representation.md), such as floaters, by combining SDS losses with depth-based constraints [S2]. The broader family of regularization approaches contrasts with progressive reconstruction techniques like [FreeNeRF](#17644-freenerf.md) and Nerfies, which restrain model complexity over time rather than adding explicit loss terms [S1, unofficial].
